claim: Macrophages (ΜΦs) are important immune effector cells that promote (M1 ΜΦs) or inhibit (M2 ΜΦs) inflammation and are involved in numerous physiological and pathogenic immune responses.
source: Macrophages (ΜΦs) are important immune effector cells that promote (M1 ΜΦs) or inhibit (M2 ΜΦs) inflammation and are involved in numerous physiological and pathogenic immune responses.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about macrophage function and phenotypes.

claim: Two-photon excited fluorescence lifetime imaging (TPE-FLIM) is a label-free noninvasive method that can visualize ΜΦs in the human dermis in vivo.
source: Here, we show that two-photon excited fluorescence lifetime imaging (TPE-FLIM), a label-free noninvasive method, can visualize ΜΦs in the human dermis in vivo.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study demonstrated through experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Human dermal ΜΦs exhibit specific TPE-FLIM properties that distinguish them from the main components of the extracellular matrix and other dermal cells.
source: We demonstrate in vitro that human dermal ΜΦs exhibit specific TPE-FLIM properties that distinguish them from the main components of the extracellular matrix and other dermal cells.
evidence: This is supported by in vitro experimental data comparing TPE-FLIM parameters of macrophages with other cell types.

claim: Machine learning identified M1 and M2 MФs with a sensitivity of 0.88±0.04 and 0.82±0.03 and a specificity of 0.89±0.03 and 0.90±0.03, respectively.
source: Additionally, machine learning identified M1 and M2 MФs with a sensitivity of 0.88±0.04 and 0.82±0.03 and a specificity of 0.89±0.03 and 0.90±0.03, respectively.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the machine learning classification algorithm developed and tested in the study.

claim: Skin ΜΦs originate from circulating monocytes.
source: Skin ΜΦs (Dong et al., 2016; Estandarte et al., 2016; Ryter, 1985) originate from circulating monocytes (Geissmann et al., 2010; Gordon and Taylor, 2005)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Skin macrophages infiltrate the dermis via the same route as monocyte-derived dendritic cells.
source: Skin ΜΦs (Dong et al., 2016; Estandarte et al., 2016; Ryter, 1985) originate from circulating monocytes (Geissmann et al., 2010; Gordon and Taylor, 2005) via the same infiltration route into the dermis as monocyte-derived dendritic cells (Schmid and Harris, 2014; Figure 1a)
evidence: This is supported by a citation and illustrated in Figure 1a.

claim: Skin ΜΦs are mainly located in the papillary and reticular dermis in close proximity to blood vessels.
source: Skin ΜΦs (Dong et al., 2016; Estandarte et al., 2016; Ryter, 1985) originate from circulating monocytes (Geissmann et al., 2010; Gordon and Taylor, 2005) via the same infiltration route into the dermis as monocyte-derived dendritic cells (Schmid and Harris, 2014; Figure 1a) and are mainly located in the papillary and reticular dermis in close proximity to blood vessels (Weber-Matthiesen and Sterry, 1990; Figure 1b–d).
evidence: This is supported by a citation and illustrated in Figures 1b-d.

claim: Skin ΜΦs have been known for more than 30 years to be abundant and heterogeneous based on their morphology, localization, and staining properties.
source: It has been known for more than 30 years that skin ΜΦs are abundant and heterogeneous, based on their morphology, localization, and staining properties (Weber-Matthiesen and Sterry, 1990).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research from 1990.

claim: M1 ΜΦs are classically activated inflammation-promoting macrophages.
source: More recently, skin ΜΦs have been classified based on their function, and they fall into two phenotypes referred to as inflammation-promoting M1-polarised ΜΦs (classically activated) and anti-inflammatory M2-polarised ΜΦs (alternatively activated) (Arango Duque and Descoteaux, 2014; Figure 1a).
evidence: This is supported by a citation and illustrated in Figure 1a.

claim: M2 ΜΦs are alternatively activated anti-inflammatory macrophages.
source: More recently, skin ΜΦs have been classified based on their function, and they fall into two phenotypes referred to as inflammation-promoting M1-polarised ΜΦs (classically activated) and anti-inflammatory M2-polarised ΜΦs (alternatively activated) (Arango Duque and Descoteaux, 2014; Figure 1a).
evidence: This is supported by a citation and illustrated in Figure 1a.

claim: M1 ΜΦs are activated by viral and bacterial infection.

evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: M1 ΜΦs are activated by interferon-γ, lipopolysaccharide (LPS), and tumor necrosis factor (TNF) through the classical activation pathway.

evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.
